rounds.response:
Primary: Conversational Design Studio (CDS); Secondary/adjacent: Constraint Negotiator (CN) — CDS is the highest‑leverage, credibility‑building bet because it directly solves engineers’ demand for editable, multi‑branch concept exploration with provenance, while CN extends CDS to the hard downstream realities (sourcing, manufacturability, adversarial checks) so we defend both ideation and execution edges versus the rigid wizard and the light chat bot.  
Memo‑ready narrative for a skeptical senior mech eng: you’re tired of linear wizards and opaque “recommendations” that break on ugly, one‑off parts; CDS delivers a controlled, episodic conversation that spawns editable CAD snippets, ranked trade‑off matrices, and an exportable audit trail so you can branch, modify, or reject ideas with full rationale and confidence bands — not a prescriptive flow or a disconnected chat log — while CN negotiates realistic supply/process tradeoffs and flags manufacturability risks you’d otherwise discover late.  
Pilot evidence to target in 2–3 months: run two 4‑week embedded pilots (one OEM/supplier design team and one high‑mix job shop) focused on 3 real edge‑case parts each, deliver 2–4 alternative concepts per part with CAD round‑trip exports, documented trade‑offs and provenance, and collect quantitative metrics (time‑to‑viable‑concept, acceptance rate of suggestions) plus structured trust/qualitative feedback.  
Key validation learning themes (hypotheses): H1 — engineers will act on or iteratively accept ≥50% of suggested alternatives when provenance and editability are provided; H2 — branchable, artifact‑linked workflows reduce time‑to‑viable‑concept versus baseline by ≥25%; H3 — explicit rationale/confidence materially increases engineers’ willingness to sign off on low‑risk changes; H4 — CN uncovers at least one supplier/process alternative per assembly that meaningfully reduces cost/lead‑time or avoids a late manufacturability blocker.  
Recommendation: greenlight the two paired pilots with a small cross‑functional team (product manager, UX, 1 CAD integration engineer, 2 data/ML engineers) and minimal on‑prem hybrid connectors + an NDA/synthetic‑data plan to protect IP while we gather the evidence above.
